channel.title: Ghosxt Blog: Managed IT & Cybersecurity for the Central Coast
channel.description: Practical IT, cybersecurity, and compliance guidance for small businesses on California's Central Coast, from an engineer with DoD infrastructure experience.

item.title: Multi-Factor Authentication for Small Business: Which Type to Use in 2026
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: SMS codes can be intercepted and push prompts can be worn down by fatigue attacks. Which type of MFA actually protects a small business, and how to roll it out.

item.title: IT Budget Planning for Small Business: A Realistic 2027 Tech Budget
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Most small business IT budgets are a guess carried over from last year. How to build a realistic 2027 tech budget: the line items owners forget, and where a vCIO fits.

item.title: Holiday Season Cybersecurity: The Small Business Prep Checklist (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Cyberattacks on small businesses spike every November and December while support teams run thin. The security checklist to run before Black Friday hits, not during it.

item.title: Fake Remote Employees: Deepfake Hiring Fraud and How to Spot It (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Fraud rings are using deepfake video and stolen identities to get hired as remote IT and admin staff. How fake remote employee scams work, the red flags in a hiring process, and the access controls that limit the damage.

item.title: IT Asset Management for Small Business: Tracking the Devices You Don't Know You Have (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Most small businesses can't say how many laptops, licenses, or old accounts they actually have. What IT asset management tracks, why it's a security control, and how to start without new software.

item.title: Penetration Testing for Small Business: What It Tests, How Often, and What It Costs (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A vulnerability scan finds what's known; a penetration test finds what's exploitable. What a pentest actually covers, realistic pricing, and how often PCI, CMMC, and cyber insurance require one.

item.title: What Is a vCIO? Virtual CIO Services for Small Business, Explained (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A vCIO sets your IT budget, roadmap, and risk priorities without a full-time salary. What a virtual CIO actually does, how it differs from IT support and managed IT, and when a small business is ready for one.

item.title: DNS Filtering for Small Business: The Cheapest Security Control You're Probably Not Using (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: DNS filtering blocks malicious and phishing sites before a browser ever loads them, for a few dollars per device a month. What it actually catches, what it doesn't, and how to turn it on without breaking anything.

item.title: Privileged Access Management for Small Business: Getting Admin Rights Under Control (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Almost everyone at a small business has more access than their job requires, and most owners have no idea how many admin accounts actually exist. What privileged access management fixes, and how to start without a big budget.

item.title: August 2026 Patch Tuesday: 400 Fixes, 3 Zero-Days, and What a Small Business Needs to Do
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: August 2026 Patch Tuesday: 400 fixes and 3 zero-days, including an actively exploited Windows flaw and the SharePoint RCE chain. What a small business should do.

item.title: Attack Surface Management for Small Business: What's Exposed to the Internet Right Now (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Old subdomains, forgotten VPN portals, an ex-employee's cloud login, a test server nobody decommissioned. What attack surface management finds, and why most small businesses have never actually looked.

item.title: Data Loss Prevention for Small Business: Stopping Data From Walking Out the Door (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Where small business data actually leaks: email, personal cloud accounts, USB drives, AI chatbots, and how to stop it with tools you already pay for.

item.title: Patch Management for Small Business: The Control Everyone Skips Until It's Too Late (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Most breaches don't exploit a mystery flaw, they exploit a vulnerability that already had a patch available. Why patch management gets skipped at small businesses, and how to build one that actually works.

item.title: Tailgating and Physical Access: The Low-Tech Breach Small Businesses Don't Plan For (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A stranger holding a box and a smile gets past your locked door more often than any firewall gets bypassed. How tailgating works and how a small business stops it.

item.title: Software Supply Chain Attacks: When a Trusted Vendor's Update Becomes Your Breach (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A single compromised update from a vendor you trust can install malware across your business with zero clicks and no phishing email. How supply chain attacks work and how to catch one.

item.title: Network Printer and Copier Security: The Unpatched Server in Your Copy Room (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A network printer or copier is a full computer with a hard drive and years of unpatched firmware, and almost nobody treats it as one. What that exposes.

item.title: POS Malware and Card Skimming: The Hidden Threat to Restaurants and Retailers (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A compromised POS system or a skimmer clipped onto a card reader can steal customer card data for months before anyone notices. How it happens and how to stop it.

item.title: Cloud Misconfiguration: The Silent Data Leak in Your Sharing Settings (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: An 'anyone with the link' share or a forgotten guest account can expose company data for months, no hacker required. How it happens and how to fix it.

item.title: Password Spray Attacks: How One Slow-Motion Guess Slips Past Lockout Policies (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Password spraying tries one common password against hundreds of accounts, so it never trips a lockout policy. How the attack works and what actually stops it.

item.title: Insider Threats: The Cybersecurity Risk Already Inside Your Business (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Most small business security spending targets outsiders, but a careless click or a departing hire's laptop does as much damage. How insider threats work.

item.title: Ransomware Negotiation: Should Your Small Business Ever Pay? (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: What actually happens during a ransomware negotiation, why paying doesn't guarantee your data back, and what a small business must settle before wiring a cent.

item.title: Social Media Account Takeover: How Hackers Hijack Your Business Facebook or Instagram Page (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A hacked Facebook or Instagram business page gets used to scam your customers or drain your ad budget. How the takeover happens and how to get it back.

item.title: IoT Device Security for Small Business: The Hidden Attack Surface (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Smart cameras, thermostats, and printers often run default passwords and years-old firmware. How IoT devices become an entry point and how to lock them down.

item.title: Fileless Malware: The Attack That Leaves Nothing for Antivirus to Find (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Fileless malware and living-off-the-land attacks run entirely in memory using tools already on your PC, so antivirus never sees a file to scan.

item.title: VoIP Toll Fraud: How a Hacked Phone System Runs Up a Five-Figure Bill Overnight (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A hacked business phone system can rack up thousands in international calls in a single weekend. How VoIP toll fraud works and how to stop it.

item.title: USB Drop Attacks: How a "Lost" Flash Drive Becomes a Ransomware Foothold (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: A USB drive left in a parking lot can hand an attacker a foothold before anyone clicks a link. How USB drop attacks work and how to stop them.

item.title: Malvertising: How Fake Software Ads Are Infecting Small Businesses (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Malicious search ads impersonate PuTTY, Zoom, and other downloads, infecting employees before the real site loads. How malvertising works.

item.title: ClickFix: The Fake CAPTCHA Attack Tricking Employees Into Infecting Their Own PC (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: ClickFix pages pose as a CAPTCHA or Zoom error, tricking employees into pasting a command into Windows Run. How it bypasses antivirus.

item.title: Evil Twin Wi-Fi: How Fake Hotspots Steal Data From Remote Workers (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Evil twin Wi-Fi hotspots copy a real network's name to intercept logins and files from remote and traveling employees. How the attack works and how to stop it.

item.title: Session Hijacking: How Stolen Cookies Let Attackers Skip Past MFA (2026)
item.dc:creator: Ulises Paiz
item.description: Session hijacking steals the cookie that proves you're logged in, letting attackers skip MFA without a password. How it works and how to stop it.
